`django/urls/base.py` holds the top-level `resolve()` function, which calls it.

- `django/urls/resolvers.py`: `URLResolver.resolve` matches its own prefix pattern against the path. It then loops over its `url_patterns` and recurses into child resolvers. As the recursion returns, it merges the captured args and kwargs from each level. It also joins the route strings and collects the namespaces. The result is a `ResolverMatch`. The `match` methods on `RoutePattern` and the regex pattern class do the per-level matching.
- `django/urls/base.py`: the public `resolve(path, urlconf)` gets the resolver for the urlconf and calls its `resolve`.

`django/template/loader_tags.py` implements this, and I found nothing else that does. I read only part of it, from the grep output, so the details below come from matching lines rather than a full read. The `BlockContext`, `BlockNode` and `ExtendsNode` classes are the ones involved. I didn't open the file to confirm the class names. Searches for `block.super` in `docs/ref/templates/builtins.txt` and `docs/topics/templates.txt` found nothing, so I'm not listing any docs.

`ExtendsNode` collects the child's `{% block %}` nodes into a block context and then renders the parent template. When the parent renders a block, `BlockNode.render` takes the child's override from that context and uses it instead. `BlockNode.super()` backs `{{ block.super }}`, which renders the parent's original content for that block.

`BlockNode.render` also sets `context["block"]` so that `block.super` can resolve.

`django/template/loader_tags.py`

`django/template/loader_tags.py`

Django's template inheritance lives in this file. `ExtendsNode` collects the child's `{% block %}` nodes and adds them to a `BlockContext`, which holds a stack of overriding blocks for each block name. When the parent template renders, `BlockNode.render` takes the most-derived override from that stack and renders it instead of the parent's own content. `BlockNode.super()` backs `{{ block.super }}`: it renders the next block up the stack, which is the parent's original content.

`django/template/loader_tags.py`

This file holds `ExtendsNode`, `BlockNode` and `BlockContext`. `ExtendsNode` gathers the child template's blocks into the `BlockContext`, so they replace the parent's blocks of the same name. When a block renders, `BlockNode` exposes the parent's original content as `block.super`. I found this by searching for `block.super` and the node class names, and I did not open the file to read the render logic itself.

`django/template/loader_tags.py`

This file holds the whole mechanism:
- `ExtendsNode.render` puts the child's blocks and then the parent's blocks into a `BlockContext`. That makes the child's version of each block the one that gets rendered.
- `BlockNode.render` pops the most-derived block from that context, renders it, and exposes it to the template as `{{ block }}`.
- `BlockNode.super()` is what `{{ block.super }}` calls. It renders the next block up the chain, which is the parent's original content, and returns it as safe output.
